topic.title: Advanced Features
topic.shortdesc: Font embedding with obfuscation, image optimization, and cover page generation in detail.

section.title: Font Embedding
section.p: Custom fonts are essential for brand consistency and professional typography. The plugin supports four font embeddingformatsfont formats: TTFTrueType (.ttf), OTFOpenType (.otf), WOFFWeb Open Font Format (.woff), and WOFF2WOFF2 (.woff2).
To embed fonts, point the epub.embed.fonts parameter at a directory containing your font files:

The legacy alias epub.embedded.fonts is also supported. The build pipeline scans the directory and auto-populates an internal epub.font.files property with the discovered files — you should not set this property manually.
The plugin automatically performs four operations:

image.alt: Four-step font pipeline: discover font files, detect family/weight/style from filenames, generate @font-face CSS and OPF manifest entries, and obfuscate with the IDPF XOR algorithm

ol.li: Discovery — scans the directory for files with .ttf, .otf, .woff, or .woff2 extensions.

Detection — parses filenames to determine the font family, weight (Thin through Black, 100–900), and style (normal, italic, oblique). For example, Merriweather-BoldItalic.woff2 is detected as family Merriweather, weight 700, style italicThe detection algorithm strips common suffixes like -Regular, -Bold, -Italic, -Light, etc. If your font files use non-standard naming, you may need to rename them..
CSS generation — produces @font-face rules in styles/epub-fonts.css, automatically linked from all content documents.

Obfuscation — if enabled, applies the font obfuscationIDPF algorithmIDPF obfuscation algorithm (per EPUB OCF 3.3 Section 4.2), XORing the first 1,040 bytes of each font file with a SHA-1 key derived from the publication identifier. An encryption.xml file is generated in META-INF/.

section.note: Font obfuscation is not encryption. It provides a minimal level of protection that satisfies most font licensing agreements, but it is trivially reversible by anyone with the publication identifier. Do not rely on it for DRM.

section.title: Image Optimization
section.p: Large images are the primary contributor to EPUB file size. The plugin's image optimizationconfigurationimage optimization pipeline can significantly reduce file sizes without visible quality loss:
The optimizer processes JPEG and PNG files recursively in the images directory:

ul.li: JPEG files are re-encoded at the specified quality level (0.0–1.0, default 0.8). Images with alpha channels are automatically converted to RGB before encoding.
PNG files are re-encoded to strip non-essential metadata (color profiles, text chunks, timestamps).
Small files below 50 KB are skipped, as the savings would be negligible.
Oversized images are scaled down to the specified maximum width while preserving aspect ratio.

section.p: Only files that become smaller after optimization are replaced; the originals are preserved if re-encoding would increase the size.

section.title: Cover Page Generation
section.p: When you provide a cover image via epub.cover.image, the plugin generates a cover pagegenerationcover page (cover.xhtml) as the first item in the spine. The cover image is also registered in the OPF manifest with the cover-image property, which reading systems use for library thumbnails.
Supported image formats include SVG, PNG, JPEG, and WebP. For best results across reading systems, use an image with a 2:3 aspect ratio (e.g., 1200 × 1800 pixels for raster formats).
section.note: SVG covers render crisply at any resolution and produce smaller file sizes than raster equivalents. They are ideal for text-heavy covers that do not require photographic imagery.
